p.hi: (Vanderlip makes gesture of despair, signifying that he has been completely beaten. Freda laughs merrily.)

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Oh, you women!

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Who is this strange lady?

div.head: FREDA
div.p: Ask him.

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: None of your business, you and your games! I quit. I've bucked myself broke against you—(Whirling on Freda.)—against all of you.
Go ahead, arrest me. It's a fake, and you know it. But go ahead.

div.head: POLICEMAN
div.p: I've only got my orders. Sorry. You'll come along peaceably?

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: You know it's a fake.

div.head: POLICEMAN
div.p: I know only my orders. Sorry.

div.head: FREDA
div.p: It's too bad you can't stop longer, but—

p.hi: (A jingling oj dog bells is heard without, and shouts of men. A knock on street door. Maid opens door. Flossie appears in doorway and enters. Sitka Charley enters at her heels and closes door. Flossie is dazzled by the lights and looks about hesitatingly. She is well frosted up. A nose-strap is across her nose. She removes nose-strap. Looks about, and sees Vanderlip. Freda starts toward her, impulsively, to receive her.)

div.head: FLOSSIE

p.hi: (Making a weak little lame run toward Vanderlip, with infinite relief in her voice.)

div.p: Floyd!

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Flossie!

p.hi: (He opens his arms and she staggers and falls into them. Her head lies on his breast for a space, while he holds her and stares helplessly around. Then she lifts her head, inviting the kiss, and perforce he bends head and kisses her.)

div.head: FLOSSIE
div.p: Oh, Floyd! Floyd!

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Dear, dear Flossie!

div.head: FLOSSIE

p.hi: (Still in his arms, but throwing her head back to look at him, in playful manner.)

div.p: You big, impatient man!

p.hi: (Vanderlip is puzzled, and only awkwardly pats her shoulder with one arm that is around her.)

div.p: You cruel, cruel man!
Couldn't wait. Couldn't let me have my night's rest and arrive in the morning fresh.

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Ah—hum—yes.

p.hi: (She puts her lips up to him and he again kisses her.)

(Sitka Charley remains inside street door. Capt. Eppingwell is restless, betraying a feeling that it is time to go. Policeman is restless. Mrs. Eppingwell and Freda, now near to each other, are looking on.)

div.head: FLOSSIE
div.p: My! What lots of dogs you must have!

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Hum, yes.

div.head: FLOSSIE
div.p: First came an Indian with six dogs. You know, the Indian with one eye.

p.hi: (Mrs. Eppingwell and Capt. Eppingwell look at each other significantly. Vanderlip, after a moment's hesitancy, nods.)

div.p: Then came the second Indian with eight dogs.

p.hi: (Mrs. Eppingwell looks inquiringly at Capt. Eppingwell, who shakes head, then each looks bepuzzlement at the other. Vanderlip, again hesitating, nods.)

div.p: And then came Sitka Charley with seven of the most magnificent dogs I ever saw. Oh, Floyd, they were just grand!

(Mrs. Eppingwell and Capt. Eppingwell look more bepuzzled than ever. Vanderlip looks across at Freda with comprehension, by his look as much as saying, "You are responsible for this." Freda smiles. Mrs. Eppingwell and Capt. Eppingwell observe the proceeding, and look at each other significantly.) We just flew along—like the wind!

div.head: VANDERLIP

p.hi: (Seeing the whole situation and lying up to it.)

div.p: I just bet you did. I knew they'd bring you in on the jump. I told them I didn't want any loafing, and... well, from the looks of it, I guess there wasn't any.

div.head: FLOSSIE
div.p: Couldn't wait a bit longer, could you, dear?

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: You just bet I couldn't.

div.head: POLICEMAN
div.p: (Unobserved by Flossie, whose back is toward him, stepping forward toward Vanderlip, the warrant still in his hand.).
Sorry—

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Give it to me.
It will be all right. You understand.

div.head: POLICEMAN

p.hi: (Nodding, pulling on mittens, and bowing very politely.)

div.p: Then I will wish you good night.

div.head: CAPT. EPPINGWELL

p.hi: (To Mrs. Eppingwell, indicating desire to go.)

div.p: We're scarcely needed here, I think.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: One moment, Archie. I'm all in a daze, and I'm curious.
Charley, the team of dogs you drove, whose were they?

div.head: FREDA

p.hi: (Who, now that the fight is over and won, is on the verge of breaking down, interrupts Sitka Charley, and speaks herself.)

div.p: Now I wish you would all go home and leave me alone. I want to go to bed.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: But I am curious, Freda, as you were curious. I want to know. I insist.

div.head: FREDA
div.p: Please, please go.

div.head: FLOSSIE

p.hi: (Who has lifted head and been regarding Freda, to Vanderlip. Loud enough for all to hear, but not too loud.)

div.p: Who is that woman?

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: Well... you see, Flossie... it's like this.

div.head: FLOSSIE
div.p: She is not a friend of yours?

div.head: VANDERLIP
div.p: No, no, of course not. You see, this is the Klondike. Things are different here than from what you've been used to, and... and...

div.head: FLOSSIE

p.hi: (Interrupting, showing in voice and demeanor comprehension of Freda's status.)

div.p: Oh, I understand. It will be better for us to go, I think.

p.hi: (They start toward street door, Vanderlip supporting Flossie around waist. She is very tired and leans heavily against him. He puts on bearskin coat, mittens, etc. He does not speak, though he nods awkwardly. As they make exit he glances back at Freda.)

div.head: FREDA
div.p: Now will you go.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: No, I insist. There has been a misunderstanding.

p.hi: (Freda, tears imminent, makes nervous exclamation, and with both hands makes nervous gesture. Turns her back, walks rapidly to front, and throws herselj into easy chair, where she sits, face up, facing audience.)

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Those dogs you drove, Charley. Whose were they?

div.head: SITKA CHARLEY

p.hi: (Hesitating, shifting weight from one leg to the other and back again, looking appealingly at back of chair in which Freda is seated.)

div.p: Me no know.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Of course you know.

div.head: SITKA CHARLEY

p.hi: (Still hesitatingly, still shifting weight back and forth, still looking appealingly at back of chair occupied by Freda.)

div.p: Maybe know, maybe not know.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Tell me.

div.head: SITKA CHARLEY
div.p: What for, all you womans? Make Sitka Charley much tired. All the time,

"Charley, tell me this, Charley, tell me that." All the time, "Charley, no tell this, Charley, no tell that." Sitka Charley tired. Sitka Charley much tired. Sitka Charley dam tired. Now Sitka Charley tell.

p.hi: (He pauses, while Mrs. Eppingwell waits expectantly, and Freda, with expressionless face, faces audience.)

div.p: Sitka Charley big fool, too. Him think you love Vanderlip. Him think Freda love Vanderlip. (Shaking head.)

No love. All the same make Vanderlip big fool. All the time all womans make all mans big fool. You say, No tell Freda. Freda say, No tell you. All right. Sitka Charley no tell. Now Sitka Charley much tired. Now him tell. Um, him drive Freda's dogs. Freda say, "Charley, bring Flossie girl much quick."

p.hi: (Looking at Mrs. Eppingwell with expression of pride, boastfully.)

div.p: Sitka Charley bring Flossie girl much quick.

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Who was the woman at the water-hole?

div.head: SITKA CHARLEY
div.p: Um Lisznayi woman.

p.hi: (Mrs. Eppingwell is surprised. Capt. Eppingwell makes dumb show of delight.)

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Archie, will you ever have faith in me again?

div.head: SITKA CHARLEY

p.hi: (Moving toward door, turning toward back of Freda's chair.)

div.p: Dogs much hungry.

p.hi: (Stops and waits, looking at Freda's chair.)

div.p: Um, me go feed dogs.

p.hi: (After regarding chair for a moment, starts on toward street door. Again stops and looks at chair.)

div.p: I go now, Freda.

div.head: FREDA

p.hi: (Not turning head, expressionless face and voice.)

div.p: Good night, Charley.

p.hi: (Mrs. Eppingwell looks toward Freda's chair, starts as though to go to Freda, hesitates, and stops. Turns upon Capt. Eppingwell and shoves him toward street door. Capt. Eppingwell makes exit. Door slams. Mrs. Eppingwell remains standing on one side of door, looking toward Freda's chair. Maid stands on other side of door, looking at Mrs. Eppingwell.)
(When door slams, Freda rises to her feet. The breakdown has come.)

div.head: FREDA
div.p: Thank God!

p.hi: (Without looking toward street door, or becoming aware that Mrs. Eppingwell still remains, Freda goes rapidly to right, to couch, sobs struggling up, her breast heaving. She sinks to floor, resting arms on couch, face buried in arms and couch, and sobs convulsively.)
(Mrs. Eppingwell comes forward and touches Freda on shoulder.)

div.head: FREDA
div.p: It is all right, Minnie. You may go to bed.

p.hi: (Mrs. Eppingwell waits a moment, sits down on couch, and rests hand on Freda's head.)

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Freda.

div.head: FREDA

p.hi: (Starting with violent surprise and looking up.)

div.p: You!

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Yes, I.

div.head: FREDA

p.hi: (Trying to be harsh, but succeeding in being only reproachful.)

div.p: I asked you to go.

p.hi: (Turns face away from Mrs. Eppingwell and looks straight forward toward audience.)

div.head: MRS. EPPINGWELL
div.p: Freda

p.hi: (Freda turns head and looks into Mrs. Eppingwell's face. Mrs. Eppingwell puts her arm around Freda's shoulder and draws her close. Freda bursts into tears and buries face in Mrs. Eppingwell's lap. Mrs. Eppingwell bends over her, soothing her.)
